target: ...the corrosion allowance brings the wall thickness of the absorber to 73 mm, and the thickness at that value governs the rest of the selection in this section. The lean solvent pump imposes no further change on the shell at this point: its duty was fixed with the hydraulics, and the wall has not been revisited since. What remains open in the mechanical design is the gasket selection for the flanged joints of the absorber. The two candidate materials are compared on temperature limit only. Pressure capability, chemical resistance and cost are not compared here, because the temperature limit is the property on which the two materials differ in a way that bears on this service, and the remaining properties were settled with the flange specification. On temperature limit the higher-rated material is preferred. The preference is narrow. It rests on the margin between the rated limit and the highest temperature the joint can reach in service, and on nothing else. The joint in question is made up and broken for inspection, and each remake seats the gasket afresh on the flange faces, so the material is asked to seal repeatedly and not once only. A material whose limit is approached in service has no margin for the excursions that accompany start-up and shutdown, when the joint temperature moves most and the seating is least settled. The lower-rated material is not set aside on its record in service, which is not in question here; it is set aside because its rated limit sits closer to the highest temperature the joint can reach, and the comparison this section was asked to make turns on that distance alone. The higher-rated material keeps a margin at the same duty, and the margin is the whole of the case for it.
